title_en: Supreme People's Court Publishes Three Typical Cases of Crimes Involving Pornography and Illegal Publications
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Release of Three Typical Cases of Pornography-Related and Illegal Publication Crimes

Case 1

Wang Tonglin et al. — crime of disseminating obscene materials

(1) Basic Facts

Defendant Wang Tonglin, male, Han ethnicity, born on April 3, 1970, super moderator of a certain pornographic website.

Defendant Yang Jianhua, male, Han ethnicity, born on October 29, 1959, super moderator of a certain pornographic website.

Defendant Huang Yong, male, Han ethnicity, born on October 31, 1989, super moderator of a certain pornographic website.

Defendant Liang Wei, male, Han ethnicity, born on September 28, 1991, super moderator of a certain pornographic website.

Defendant Wang Xiqun, male, Han ethnicity, born on December 21, 1975, moderator of a certain pornographic website.

Defendant Li Hengjun, male, Han ethnicity, born on September 13, 1990, super moderator of a certain pornographic website.

Defendant Xi Liangliang, male, Han ethnicity, born on February 1, 1983, moderator of a certain pornographic website.

Defendant Ye Bo, male, Han ethnicity, born on June 9, 1987, super moderator of a certain pornographic website.

Defendant Hao Zhipeng, male, Han ethnicity, born on January 20, 1991, moderator of a certain pornographic website.

Defendant Han Jinbo, male, Han ethnicity, born on May 3, 1988, moderator of a certain pornographic website.

Between May 2011 and December 2011, the defendants Wang Tonglin, Yang Jianhua, Huang Yong, Liang Wei, Wang Xiqun, Li Hengjun, Xi Liangliang, Ye Bo, Hao Zhipeng, and Han Jinbo, knowing that a certain pornographic website created by others was a website for disseminating obscene electronic information, nonetheless successively applied to become moderators or super moderators of that website, and respectively managed the sections designated by the website, allowing or tolerating others to post obscene electronic information in the sections they managed. The specific facts are as follows: From June 3, 2011 to January 1, 2012, Wang Tonglin allowed or tolerated others to post 6,597 obscene electronic images and 2,441 obscene novels in the section he managed, totaling 9,038 items. From May 10, 2011 to February 15, 2012, Yang Jianhua allowed or tolerated others to post 8,717 obscene electronic images in the section he managed. From November 16, 2011 to February 15, 2012, Huang Yong allowed or tolerated others to post 8,406 obscene electronic images in the section he managed. From July 11, 2011 to February 15, 2012, Liang Wei allowed or tolerated others to post 8,285 obscene electronic images in the section he managed. From June 27, 2011 to December 31, 2011, Wang Xiqun allowed or tolerated others to post 565 obscene videos in the section he managed. From November 11, 2011 to January 1, 2012, Li Hengjun allowed or tolerated others to post 349 obscene videos in the section he managed. From June 13, 2011 to February 15, 2012, Xi Liangliang allowed or tolerated others to post 3,359 obscene novels in the section he managed. From July 14, 2011 to February 17, 2012, Ye Bo allowed or tolerated others to post 3,128 obscene electronic images in the section he managed. From August 21, 2011 to December 29, 2011, Hao Zhipeng allowed or tolerated others to post 2,448 obscene electronic images in the section he managed. From July 11, 2011 to January 7, 2012, Han Jinbo allowed or tolerated others to post 121 obscene videos in the section he managed.

(2) Judgment

This case was adjudicated by the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, in accordance with law.

The court held that the defendants Wang Tonglin, Yang Jianhua, Huang Yong, Liang Wei, Wang Xiqun, Li Hengjun, Xi Liangliang, Ye Bo, Hao Zhipeng, and Han Jinbo, on the internet, allowed or tolerated others to post obscene electronic information in the website sections they managed, and the circumstances were serious. Their actions constituted the crime of disseminating obscene materials. After being brought to justice, each defendant truthfully confessed the criminal facts and voluntarily pleaded guilty, which could be given a lighter punishment according to law. Accordingly, the judgment was rendered as follows: Defendant Wang Tonglin was convicted of the crime of disseminating obscene materials and sentenced to ten months' fixed-term imprisonment; defendant Yang Jianhua was convicted of the crime of disseminating obscene materials and sentenced to ten months' fixed-term imprisonment; defendant Huang Yong was convicted of the crime of disseminating obscene materials and sentenced to ten months' fixed-term imprisonment; defendant Liang Wei was convicted of the crime of disseminating obscene materials and sentenced to ten months' fixed-term imprisonment; defendant Wang Xiqun was convicted of the crime of disseminating obscene materials and sentenced to nine months' fixed-term imprisonment; defendant Li Hengjun was convicted of the crime of disseminating obscene materials and sentenced to eight months' fixed-term imprisonment; defendant Xi Liangliang was convicted of the crime of disseminating obscene materials and sentenced to seven months' fixed-term imprisonment; defendant Ye Bo was convicted of the crime of disseminating obscene materials and sentenced to seven months' fixed-term imprisonment; defendant Hao Zhipeng was convicted of the crime of disseminating obscene materials and sentenced to six months' fixed-term imprisonment, suspended for one year; defendant Han Jinbo was convicted of the crime of disseminating obscene materials and sentenced to six months' criminal detention, suspended for one year.

Case 2

Wang Qinggang — crime of copyright infringement

(1) Basic Facts

Defendant Wang Qinggang, male, Han ethnicity, born on April 8, 1977, self-employed.

From the end of 2007 to the present, defendant Wang Qinggang successively and repeatedly printed or purchased a large number of pirated supplementary teaching materials from Xinxiang, Henan Province; Baoding and Hejian, Hebei Province; and elsewhere, for wholesale and sale. On October 13, 2011, the Taiyuan Municipal Cultural Market Administrative Comprehensive Law Enforcement Brigade conducted a concentrated seizure at three warehouses where Wang Qinggang stored goods, located in Shuiyu Village, Gangdao Village, and near the north gate of Shanxi University on Xuefu Street, Taiyuan City. A total of 308,403 copies of student supplementary teaching materials awaiting sale were seized on site. Upon appraisal, 78,044 copies were identified as infringing and pirated supplementary teaching materials.

(2) Judgment

This case was adjudicated by the Yingze District People's Court of Taiyuan, Shanxi Province, in accordance with law.

The court held that defendant Wang Qinggang, for the purpose of profit, without permission from the copyright owner, reproduced and distributed their written works. The circumstances were particularly serious, infringing upon the state's copyright management system. His actions constituted the crime of copyright infringement. As the holder of the infringing products, Wang Qinggang was apprehended before the infringing products could be sold, constituting an attempted crime, which may be given a mitigated punishment compared to a completed crime. Wang Qinggang truthfully confessed his crimes and could be given a lighter sentence. Accordingly, the judgment was rendered as follows: Defendant Wang Qinggang was convicted of the crime of copyright infringement and sentenced to two years' fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 250,000.

Case 3

Zhang Wenkun et al. — crime of illegal business operations

(1) Basic Facts

Defendant Zhang Wenkun, male, Han ethnicity, born on March 15, 1963, unemployed.

Defendant Xu Yanliang, male, Han ethnicity, born on July 17, 1968, unemployed.

Defendant Li Bai'e, female, Han ethnicity, born on March 8, 1959, farmer.

In the second half of 2009, defendant Zhang Wenkun purchased underground "Mark Six" code books from co-defendant Zhang Chunying and retailed them in Dangyang City, Hubei Province. Starting from February 2011, Zhang Wenkun purchased underground "Mark Six" code book materials from Zhang Chunying and from places such as Guangzhou City and Shantou City, Guangdong Province, for wholesale and retail. Specifically, he wholesale-supplied a total of 22,222 copies of various underground "Mark Six" code book materials to defendant Xu Yanliang and co-defendant Li Jin'e via logistics consignment, with a total sales amount of RMB 125,725.

Defendant Xu Yanliang and his wife Li Jin'e, starting from 2008, purchased underground "Mark Six" code book materials from a person surnamed Lao in Pingjiang County, Hunan Province. Starting from the second half of 2009, they also purchased underground "Mark Six" code book materials from defendant Zhang Wenkun and from places such as Shantou City via logistics transportation. In 2009, they purchased a minivan for transporting the underground "Mark Six" code book materials. After Xu Yanliang purchased the code book materials, he wholesale-supplied or retailed them to defendant Li Bai'e, as well as to persons including Li Yan'e, Li Yingchun, Li Liyun, and Yang An'an in Tongcheng County, Hubei Province; Li Wenjie in Xianning, Hubei Province; and persons in Chongyang, Jiangxi Xiushui, and other places. In total, he wholesale-supplied or retailed 65,797 copies of underground "Mark Six" code book materials and 500 copies of code newspapers, with a total sales amount of RMB 181,461.40.

Starting from the second half of 2008, defendant Li Bai'e purchased underground "Mark Six" code book materials from defendant Xu Yanliang by paying cash or on credit, and set up a stall in the vegetable market in Juanshui Town, Tongcheng County, to sell them. The sales amount was RMB 65,625.

(2) Judgment

This case was adjudicated by the Tongcheng County People's Court of Hubei Province in accordance with law.

The court held that defendants Zhang Wenkun, Xu Yanliang, and Li Bai'e, without authorization, sold illegal publications. The circumstances were serious, infringing upon the market management order. Their actions constituted the crime of illegal business operations. Given that defendants Xu Yanliang and Li Bai'e showed signs of remorse and proactively paid part of the fines, a lighter punishment could be given as deemed appropriate. Accordingly, the judgment was rendered as follows: Defendant Zhang Wenkun was convicted of the crime of illegal business operations and sentenced to two years' fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 40,000; defendant Xu Yanliang was convicted of the crime of illegal business operations and sentenced to two years' fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 60,000; defendant Li Bai'e was convicted of the crime of illegal business operations and sentenced to ten months' fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 20,000.
